programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: The friends are very excited to stay with Marvin in the Bat Cave - it's going to be so much fun! When they get to the cave, the bats are sound asleep, hibernating for the winter. The friends will have to be super quiet so they don't wake them up... but it's difficult to keep quiet when everyone's playing together. Tha na caraidean air bhioran a bhith fuireach còmh' ri Marvin ann an Uamh nan Ialtag – bidh e cho spòrsail! Nuair a ruigeas 'ad an uamh, tha na h-ialtagan nan suain, a' cadal tron gheamhradh. Feumaidh gach caraid a bhith air leth sàmhach gus nach dùisg ear 'ad...ach chan eil sin soirbh, nuair a tha gach neach ri cluich còmhla.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Baba and Lala have found something very exciting - a great big dandelion puff! When they blow the seeds away, they are very disappointed that there is no more 'fluffy'. Mama spots one seed left, and together they plant it outside the burrow to watch it grow. Baba and Lala decide to watch over the dandelion until it turns into a 'fluffy' - but they must wait for a long time for a new one to grow. Lorg baba is Lala rudeigin air leth sònraicht' – tòc mòr beàrnan-brìde! Nuiar a shèideas 'ad an sìol air falbh, tha iad glè thàmailteach nach eil an còrr “giobag” ann. Tha Mamaidh a' faicinn aon t-sìol air fhàgail, 's cruinn còmhla, tha iad ga chuir ri taobh na faiche, gus a bhith ga fhaicinn a' fàs. Tha Baba is Lala a' co-dhùnadh sùil a chumail air gus am fàs e gu bhith na “ghiobag” - ach feumar fuireach greis 'son fàs a thoirt air fear ùr.

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Tha Fuigheag a’ cluich le rudeigin beag spòrsail a lorg e. Feumaidh Boban obrachadh a-mach cò às a thàinig an rud agus an uairsin a thilleadh air ais. Fuigheag is playing with something he’s found. Boban must work out where the item has come from and return it.

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Bidh Linda a’ tadhal air Meaban is Moo gus dùbhlain spòrsail a chur romhpa. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha i ag iarraidh orra trì rudan òir a lorg. Cha deach gu math dha Meaban a’ lorg òr a-muigh ach saoil am bi ionmhas ri lorg am measg an trealaich sa bhothan? Linda visits Meaban and Moo to set them fun challenges. In this programme, she tasks them with finding three gold items. Meaban has no luck finding gold outside, but perhaps there is treasure to be found amongst the junk in the hut?

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: Tha Linda NicLeòid agus a caraidean a’ dèanamh bonnaich-èisg bhlasta. Linda and her friends make tasty fishcakes.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Mìcheal Hill a’ leughadh Na Trioblaidean aig Sioraf. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Jory John, a dhealbhachadh le Lane Smith agus eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Mòrag Stiùbhart. A bedtime story for young children. Michael Hill reads Na Trioblaidean aig Sioraf. The book was written by Jory John, illustrated by Lane Smith and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Tha Stella ‘son ‘s gum bi a h-athair mar na h-athraichean eile aig ball-coise – ach abair gu bheil daoine amharasach nuair a tha e a’ nochdadh gun a' chrùn air. Stella wants her father to be like the other dads at football, but there is much suspicion when he appears without his crown on.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Nuair tha picnic rìoghail dol a ghabhail àite sa phàirc, tha Stella air a dearg nàrachadh, gun fhios nach fhaic a caraidean i an sin. Stella is really embarrassed in case friends see her when she is with her family at a royal picnic in the park.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Chan eil na Bògaisean neo na Gumbalan a’ faireachdainn gu math oir tha ’ad a’ fulang le biorgadh bodhaig. Feumar obrachadh le chèile airson leighis a lorg. Saoil am bi e comasach dhaibh seo a dhèanamh? The Bògaisean and the Gumbals are feeling unwell today as they’re suffering from boggle twitches. They must work together to find a cure. Will it be possible?

programme.title: The Deep/An Doimhne
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Na Neachdan ann an Triantan Bhermuda, chan eil laghannan fiosaigs ag obrachadh mar bu chòir, tha iad steigte ann. Ach, le taic bho Jeffrey, tha iad a' lorg fuasgladh When the Neachdan are in the Bermuda Triangle, the laws of physics don’t seem to apply. What’s more, they’re stuck there. But with help from Jeffrey, they find a solution.

programme.title: Bus Ghlaschu/Glasgow Bus
programme.desc: Tha seinneadair Lorraine McIntosh à comhlan Deacon Blue eòlach air Bus Ghlaschu. Chi sinn Lorraine dol air ais a Dhùn nan Gall far a bheil ceangal teaghlaich aice. Lorraine MacIntosh, from Deacon Blue, knows the Glasgow bus well. Join the singer as she shares her connections to Donegal.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: We meet Gaelic learner Caroline Quinn from Trinidad and Tobago, while Calum Maclean is in Portmahomack, Easter Ross, learning about his heritage.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Somhairle Spins
programme.desc: Às dèidh toiseach tòiseachaidh dùbhlanach, lean Somhairle agus Innes orra a’ rothaireachd air a Bhadger Divide, far an tàinig iad tarsainn air duilgheadasan meacanaigeach; uisge trom; geàrr-rathaidean; tionndadh ceàrr agus bagannan caillte! Thàinig an rothaiche agus an neach-gleidhidh chlàran, Kerry Nic a’Phì, còmhla riutha airson earrann. After a tough start, Somhairle and Innes continue riding the Badger Divide, where they encounter mechanical issues, torrential rain, shortcuts, wrong turns and lost baggage! They’re joined for a section by record-holder, cyclist Kerry MacPhee.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.desc: After years of unhappiness, mill worker Mairead finally walks out of her decades-long marriage and into the arms of the person she loves - hotel owner Cairistiona. However, as the women agree to wait for the right time to tell Mairead’s husband Boyd they are together, little do they know there’s someone watching from the shadows. Às dèidh bliadhnaichean de mhì-thoileachas, tha neach-obrach na muilne, Mairead, a’ fàgail an duine aice às dèidh bliadhnaichean fada pòsta airson a bhith còmhla ris an neach air a bheil gaol aice – Cairistìona, aig a bheil an taigh-òsta. Ach, ged a tha na boireannaich agaontachadh feitheamh gus innse dha Boyd, an duine aig Mairead, gu bheil iad còmhla – ‘s beag a dh’fhios a th’ aca gu bheil cuideigin ‘san dorchadas gan coimhead. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Alba fon Talamh/Scotland Underground
programme.desc: Calum starts his underground tour in the north west of Scotland. With help from local experts, he explores the incredible cave networks of Applecross. Looking at how man has harnessed underground resources, Calum explores the Nevis Tunnels, the aluminium smelter in Fort William and the globally unique Lochaline sand mine. Tha Calum a’ tòiseachadh air a thuras fon talamh ann an Iar-thuath na h-Alba. Le cuideachadh bho eòlaichean-uamha ionadail, rannsachaidh e lìonraidhean uamhan iongantach na Comraich. Chithear mar a tha mac an duine air feum a dhèanamh de ghoireasan fon talamh fhad ’s a nì Calum rannsachadh air Tunailean Nibheis agus leaghadair aluiminium a’ Ghearasdain, cho math ri mèinne gainmhich ann an Loch Àlainn a tha gun shamhail san t-saoghal. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Samhradh air Sàl
programme.desc: Angus Mackay is joined by his daughter Ruth as they go to sea on a spectacular summer's day. Along the way they encounter a large pod of dolphins who take great delight in racing their small boat. Then it’s time for fishing and chat about the formative role of fishing in Ruth’s upbringing. Anns an dàrna prògram mu dheireadh san t-sreath, tha nighean Aonghais, Rut, còmhla ris agus iad aig muir air latha samhraidh eireachdail. Air an t-slighe, coinnichidh iad ri buidheann leumadairean-mara a tha dannsa mun eathar. Às dèidh sin, tha an t-àm ann airson iasgach agus còmhradh mun bhuaidh a bh’ aig iasgach air beatha Ruth.

programme.title: Port
programme.desc: Sreath aithriseach ciùil ùr ann an cuideachd Julie Fowlis agus Muireann NicAmhlaoibh, 's iad air slighe rannsachaidh mu na freumhan aca fhèin, a-nochd ann am Baile Àth-Cliath. Nì Port taisbeanadh air na ceanglaichean dualchais a tha eadar dithis a tha air a bhith na 'n caraidean 's na 'n companaich-ciùil fad iomadh bliadhna. Tha an seinneadair Darren MacIlleathain agus am pìobaire Carole-Ann NicAoidh a' tadhal air grunnd ionadan cliùiteach ann am Baile Àth-Cliath ann an cuideachd Julie is Muireann. Musical documentary with Julie Fowlis and Muireann NicAmhlaoibh as they take to the road to explore their shared musical roots. In Dublin, Port reveals their shared musical heritage. Port celebrates the common musical heritage of the longtime friends and collaborators as they cross borders and traditions between the west of Ireland and the Western Isles, meeting and playing with friends and musicians en route. Singer Darren MacLean and piper Carole-Anne MacKay join our musical hosts for a tour of several iconic venues. True to form, Dublin doesn't disappoint and gives up some musical gems.

programme.title: Fergie, The Ceilidh King
programme.desc: Program a tha a’ dèanamh luaidh air am fear-ciùil Fergie Dòmhnallach à Loch Abar a chaochail na bu thràithe am-bliadhna. Lìon e tallaichean-baile air feadh Alba le daoine ga ghabhail fhèin agus a stoidhle ciùil rin cridheachan. Agus ge bith càit am biodh Fergie, bhiodh seanchas agus craic am pailteas! Bha tuigse air leth aige air a’ cheangal a bha eadar daoine agus ceòl agus, leis an tuigse sin agus a sgil fhèin, bha na puirt aige tarraingeach do dh’iomadh ginealach airson 60 bliadhna. B’ e an Ceilidh King, fear-ciùil air an robh meas aig daoine fad is farsaing agus gheibh sinn sealladh air an duine fhèin bho theaghlach, a charaidean agus bho luchd-ciùil eile a bha eòlach air. A tribute to Lochaber musician Fergie MacDonald who died in 2024. Fergie filled halls and captured hearts across Scotland with his distinctive West Coast musical style, as well as his infectious sense of humour. With a unique understanding of how people connect with music, he sustained a 60-year career and his popularity spanned generations. We hear from musicians, friends and family about what made the Ceilidh King one of Scotland’s most loved musicians. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: Bracaistean falainn a th’ aig na seòid is Ruairidh le trioblaidean cridhe. The lads focus on healthy breakfasts after Roddy’s heart condition diagnosis.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Travels with Pevsner
programme.desc: With Nikolaus Pevsner's Buildings of England in hand, Michael Bracewell explores the architecture of Surrey. Amongst the places he visits are Polesden Lacey, Whitely Village and The Beehive at Gatwick Airport.

programme.title: Inside Classical
programme.desc: The BBC Philharmonic Orchestra and conductor Ben Gernon perform Bruch’s First Violin Concerto and Dvorak’s Symphony No 9, 'From the New World'. Bruch’s romantic violin concerto is performed by Jennifer Pike, who first gained attention in 2002, when at 12 years old, she won the BBC Young Musician competition. She is now in demand as a soloist around the world. Dvorak wrote his Ninth Symphony on a journey of musical discovery around America. It takes inspiration from both native and African-American melodies, and is a cinematic display of orchestral colour that captures the spirit of new discovery.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take you so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. It is all about making connections between things which may appear, at first glance, not to be connected at all.

programme.title: Lost Cities of the Ancients
programme.desc: In the Lambeyeque valley in northern Peru lies a strange lost world - the forgotten ruins of 250 mysterious pyramids, including some of the biggest on the planet, colossal structures made out of mud bricks. Long ago, the Lambeyeque people were haunted by a terrible fear and believed that building pyramids was essential to their survival. Their obsession reached its height at a city called Tucume, an eerie place of 26 pyramids standing side by side, the last pyramids this civilisation created before they vanished forever. What was the fear that drove these people to build so many pyramids, what were they for and why did the whole civilisation suddenly vanish? This film captures the moments when archaeologists at the site uncovered a mass of bodies of human sacrifice victims, following a trail of clues into the dark story of Tucume. It recreates the strange rituals of the people of the valley, revealing a civilisation whose obsession to build pyramids eventually turned to horror, until Tucume finally vanished in a bloody frenzy of human sacrifice.

programme.title: Da Vinci: The Lost Treasure
programme.desc: Leonardo da Vinci is considered by many to be one of the greatest artists who ever lived. Yet his reputation rests on only a handful of pictures - including the world's most famous painting, the Mona Lisa. As the National Gallery in London prepares to open its doors on a remarkable exhibition of Leonardo's work, Fiona Bruce travels to Florence, Milan, Paris and Warsaw to uncover the story of this enigmatic genius - and to New York, where she is given an exclusive preview of a sensational discovery: a new Leonardo.

programme.title: British Art at War: Bomberg, Sickert and Nash
programme.desc: In the years preceding 1914, David Bomberg, Walter Sickert and Paul Nash set out to paint a new world, but, as the century unfolded, found themselves working in the rubble. Walter Sickert's early career as an actor is long forgotten and he's now remembered for his art. But he never left the stage behind. Always shape-shifting between roles, Sickert's appearance never stayed still. And his art, too, was in perpetual transformation. Dazzlingly original, deeply unsettling, poised on the brink of violence. For most, proof that Sickert is the godfather of modern British art, but for a few at the fringes, evidence he's Jack the Ripper. But Sickert was no perpetrator, just an unflinching witness, notably, to the cataclysm of World War One. Too old to fight in Flanders, Sickert painted edgy, compelling, subtle pictures of those who'd been left behind. He painted people trying to get on with lives that were being shattered by the conflict. Almost alone of his generation, Sickert truly understood that the theatre of war was not confined to the trenches.

programme.title: An Art Lovers' Guide
programme.desc: In the first of a series of city adventures, Janina Ramirez and Alastair Sooke head to Lisbon, rapidly becoming one of Europe’s most popular tourist destinations. Winding through the city’s cobbled streets, from its steep hills to the picturesque shore line, the cultural riches they encounter reveal the city's fascinating history. From a spectacular monument to the maritime globetrotting of Portugal’s golden age and the work of a photographer documenting the city's large African population, they discover a complex history of former glories and a darker, slave-trading past. Their journey also uncovers the impact of 20th-century dictatorship on the city's artistic and cultural life, through the work of contemporary artists Paula Rego and Joana Vasconcelos. And they discover how the city's location on the west coast of Europe, looking out to the Atlantic, has shaped the cosmopolitan spirit of the city. In one of the city's Fado clubs, Alastair and Nina enjoy the popular Portuguese folk music, whose beautiful melodies celebrate a yearning for home, once sung by sailors dreaming of their return.

programme.desc: In the 18th century, trade and conquest funds an explosion of creativity, and art stirs a growing social conscience.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: A dispute around the latest series of I'm a Celebrity...Get Me Out of Here has drawn attention to how reality television is edited. Some contestants have said that footage was cut in a misleading way, affecting how they were shown on screen. The broadcaster ITV has said the programme reflects events fairly and accurately. Lauren Morris, Culture News Editor at The Independent, alongside reality television producers Donald Clarke and Rob Davis, discuss the processes and standards used in production. King Charles' state visit to the US has taken place at a time of diplomatic tension, following criticism from President Trump over the UK's position on the war with Iran. The visit, the first by a British monarch in nearly two decades, involved a series of carefully planned public events and took place under heightened security. Sean Coughlan, Royal Correspondent at BBC News, and Jack Blanchard, author of POLITICO's Playbook newsletter, outline their reporting approaches and editorial context.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: AI Decoded speaks to leading tech podcaster Scott Galloway about the growing controversy surrounding Anthropic's latest AI model, Claude Mythos. During testing, the system uncovered thousands of hidden vulnerabilities in the software underpinning most of the world's computers - prompting Anthropic to decide it was too dangerous to release. The company says Mythos can outperform humans at certain hacking and cyber security tasks, raising fresh concerns among regulators, lawmakers and financial institutions about the risks to global digital infrastructure.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the courier company that customers say is still letting them down – despite past promises made on the programme. Also in this episode, how secure is your self-storage unit? The team hears from one customer whose unit was broken into. And in the advice clinic, the team heads to Mansfield to meet the second-hand car owner whose vehicle was subject to a recall – so why was she left facing a £1,000 bill when it broke down?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A trio of rundown flats in Glasgow, London and Bournemouth are given the wow factor by family-developing teams who know how to turn unloved properties into desirable homes.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion buckles up in a vintage American muscle car to take a spin around one of Britain’s fastest racetracks. At 1.85 miles long, Castle Combe in Wiltshire is a popular circuit for vintage racing cars and has hosted some of the world’s motor racing greats. Christina rides shotgun with noise-monitoring officer Dave Hensley to learn about the history of the track and why drivers need to have their wits about them as they navigate its hair-raising straights and bends. Motoring around an antiques fair in Devon are two teams of families. In red are dad and daughter Alan and Maisie, guided by antiques expert Ben Cooper. Their opponents in blue are mum and daughter Denise and Amy, with expert Gary Pe. Alan kicks off the reds’ shop by picking out a contemporary glass vase, but Ben doesn’t see a profit in it. Meanwhile, a pair of miniature wooden doll's chairs catch Denise’s eye, but does Gary think they’ll bring a big return? Down the road from Castle Combe, auctioneer Tim Weeks gives Christina his estimates of the teams’ items. One bonus buy particularly impresses Tim, but will it fulfil its auction potential?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Rav Wilding and Nick Stapleton are back, working with ethical hacker Jim Browning to fight live scams in action and stop people across the country from paying out. The team are on the trail of a group of cryptocurrency scammers, who claim that their victims have previously lost large quantities of now-valuable crypto. All they need to do to release the funds is pay a fee up front. But the victim in question is unreachable – and the ground team might be too far away to warn him.

programme.title: Dinosaurs: The Final Day with David Attenborough
programme.desc: David Attenborough brings to life, in unprecedented detail, the last days of the dinosaurs. Palaeontologist Robert DePalma has made an incredible discovery in a prehistoric graveyard: fossilised creatures, astonishingly well preserved, that could help change our understanding of the last days of the dinosaurs. Evidence from his site records the day when an asteroid bigger than Mount Everest devastated our planet and caused the extinction of the dinosaurs. Based on brand new evidence, witness the catastrophic events of that day play out minute by minute.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from the largest town in Dorset want to escape the urban sprawl to establish a new country life in Devon, and Sonali Shah is on hand to help them kick-start their property search. Sonali also learns the importance of the role local newspapers play in keeping their communities connected and informed.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Barbara, Gareth, Rebecca and Iain – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Angela Scanlon for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: The One Show
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and JB Gill bring you the stories that matter from across the country.

programme.title: The Marvellous Miniature Workshop
programme.desc: Sara Cox and miniaturist Hannah Lemon recreate Manchester’s Crumpsall Library for Leah, a retired social worker who met her late husband there as a teenager. Though the library now lies derelict, Hannah’s intricate model - parquet floors, stained-glass and even Neil’s school cap - brings back its splendour and the love story at its heart.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Nicola receives a shock, Phil and Sam support a loved one, and Ian desperately tries to gain extra votes.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: Heat 3 is upon us, which means one thing: six exciting new amateur cooks have left their home kitchens ready to compete for one of four coveted MasterChef aprons.

programme.title: Mint
programme.desc: Reeling from a sudden loss, Shannon lashes out at her family. Only Ollie can offer her some comfort in the form of a dodgy vape. When Shannon’s day takes a surreal turn, she reconnects with herself and confronts her fears. But Dylan’s return snaps her back into a painful reality.

programme.title: Mint
programme.desc: Dylan’s new life brings moments of comfort, but he also finds it challenging in a way he never saw coming. His old coping mechanisms no longer work, and he’s forced to ask himself what he truly wants. A conversation with Luke reminds him what’s at stake and what actually matters. Meanwhile, Cat seeks clarity from her son, hoping to understand the future she wants for herself and her family.

programme.desc: Richard Ayoade hosts, with guest panellists actor and comedian Stephen Mangan and journalist Ava Santina Evans joining team captains Paul Merton and Ian Hislop as they delve into the news.

programme.title: Making Life on Earth: Attenborough's Greatest Adventure
programme.desc: In 1976, David Attenborough embarked on his most ambitious project ever, Life on Earth. No-one had ever attempted a natural history series on this scale before, and David’s reputation was on the line. This is the remarkable story behind the BBC’s most famous wildlife blockbuster. A three-year, hair-raising odyssey around the world, travelling to 40 countries and filming over 600 species, including the famous mountain gorillas. First broadcast in 1979 and watched by 500 million people, it launched David Attenborough’s career as the most successful and influential wildlife film-maker of our time.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the courier company that customers say is still letting them down – despite past promises made on the programme. Also in this episode, how secure is your self-storage unit? The team hears from one customer whose unit was broken into. And in the advice clinic, the team heads to Mansfield to meet the second-hand car owner whose vehicle was subject to a recall – so why was she left facing a £1,000 bill when it broke down?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A trio of rundown flats in Glasgow, London and Bournemouth are given the wow factor by family-developing teams who know how to turn unloved properties into desirable homes.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion buckles up in a vintage American muscle car to take a spin around one of Britain’s fastest racetracks. At 1.85 miles long, Castle Combe in Wiltshire is a popular circuit for vintage racing cars and has hosted some of the world’s motor racing greats. Christina rides shotgun with noise-monitoring officer Dave Hensley to learn about the history of the track and why drivers need to have their wits about them as they navigate its hair-raising straights and bends. Motoring around an antiques fair in Devon are two teams of families. In red are dad and daughter Alan and Maisie, guided by antiques expert Ben Cooper. Their opponents in blue are mum and daughter Denise and Amy, with expert Gary Pe. Alan kicks off the reds’ shop by picking out a contemporary glass vase, but Ben doesn’t see a profit in it. Meanwhile, a pair of miniature wooden doll's chairs catch Denise’s eye, but does Gary think they’ll bring a big return? Down the road from Castle Combe, auctioneer Tim Weeks gives Christina his estimates of the teams’ items. One bonus buy particularly impresses Tim, but will it fulfil its auction potential?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Rav Wilding and Nick Stapleton are back, working with ethical hacker Jim Browning to fight live scams in action and stop people across the country from paying out. The team are on the trail of a group of cryptocurrency scammers, who claim that their victims have previously lost large quantities of now-valuable crypto. All they need to do to release the funds is pay a fee up front. But the victim in question is unreachable – and the ground team might be too far away to warn him.

programme.title: Dinosaurs: The Final Day with David Attenborough
programme.desc: David Attenborough brings to life, in unprecedented detail, the last days of the dinosaurs. Palaeontologist Robert DePalma has made an incredible discovery in a prehistoric graveyard: fossilised creatures, astonishingly well preserved, that could help change our understanding of the last days of the dinosaurs. Evidence from his site records the day when an asteroid bigger than Mount Everest devastated our planet and caused the extinction of the dinosaurs. Based on brand new evidence, witness the catastrophic events of that day play out minute by minute.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from the largest town in Dorset want to escape the urban sprawl to establish a new country life in Devon, and Sonali Shah is on hand to help them kick-start their property search. Sonali also learns the importance of the role local newspapers play in keeping their communities connected and informed.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Barbara, Gareth, Rebecca and Iain – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Angela Scanlon for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

At 1.85 miles long, Castle Combe in Wiltshire is a popular circuit for vintage racing cars and has hosted some of the world’s motor racing greats. Christina rides shotgun with noise-monitoring officer Dave Hensley to learn about the history of the track and why drivers need to have their wits about them as they navigate its hair-raising straights and bends. Motoring around an antiques fair in Devon are two teams of families. In red are dad and daughter Alan and Maisie, guided by antiques expert Ben Cooper. Their opponents in blue are mum and daughter Denise and Amy, with expert Gary Pe. Alan kicks off the reds’ shop by picking out a contemporary glass vase, but Ben doesn’t see a profit in it. Meanwhile, a pair of miniature wooden doll's chairs catch Denise’s eye, but does Gary think they’ll bring a big return? Down the road from Castle Combe, auctioneer Tim Weeks gives Christina his estimates of the teams’ items. One bonus buy particularly impresses Tim, but will it fulfil its auction potential?

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Rav Wilding and Nick Stapleton are back, working with ethical hacker Jim Browning to fight live scams in action and stop people across the country from paying out. The team are on the trail of a group of cryptocurrency scammers, who claim that their victims have previously lost large quantities of now-valuable crypto. All they need to do to release the funds is pay a fee up front. But the victim in question is unreachable – and the ground team might be too far away to warn him.

programme.title: Dinosaurs: The Final Day with David Attenborough
programme.desc: David Attenborough brings to life, in unprecedented detail, the last days of the dinosaurs. Palaeontologist Robert DePalma has made an incredible discovery in a prehistoric graveyard: fossilised creatures, astonishingly well preserved, that could help change our understanding of the last days of the dinosaurs. Evidence from his site records the day when an asteroid bigger than Mount Everest devastated our planet and caused the extinction of the dinosaurs. Based on brand new evidence, witness the catastrophic events of that day play out minute by minute.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Barbara, Gareth, Rebecca and Iain – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Making Life on Earth: Attenborough's Greatest Adventure
programme.desc: In 1976, David Attenborough embarked on his most ambitious project ever, Life on Earth. No-one had ever attempted a natural history series on this scale before, and David’s reputation was on the line. This is the remarkable story behind the BBC’s most famous wildlife blockbuster. A three-year, hair-raising odyssey around the world, travelling to 40 countries and filming over 600 species, including the famous mountain gorillas. First broadcast in 1979 and watched by 500 million people, it launched David Attenborough’s career as the most successful and influential wildlife film-maker of our time.

programme.desc: On patrol in the city centre, Adam and Nigel receive reports of men fleeing police. As they round the corner, they spot them legging it. Adam takes pursuit, tackles and detains one of the suspects. A few minutes later, unbelievably, he must do it again, as the man bursts out of the police car, trying to escape. Back at the station, Anna and Perri can’t resist the temptation to hide the boss’s car, temporarily. Meanwhile, the whole team leap into action when a stolen car fails to stop for Adam. When the driver runs off, Dave relies on his years of experience and pays a visit to a serial car thief matching the driver’s description. While the Peelers wait for CCTV footage to come in, the suspect tells Stephen about his prolific criminal past, his hatred of police and struggles with addiction.

Based on brand new evidence, witness the catastrophic events of that day play out minute by minute.

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Barbara, Gareth, Rebecca and Iain – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion buckles up in a vintage American muscle car to take a spin around one of Britain’s fastest racetracks. At 1.85 miles long, Castle Combe in Wiltshire is a popular circuit for vintage racing cars and has hosted some of the world’s motor racing greats. Christina rides shotgun with noise-monitoring officer Dave Hensley to learn about the history of the track and why drivers need to have their wits about them as they navigate its hair-raising straights and bends. Motoring around an antiques fair in Devon are two teams of families. In red are dad and daughter Alan and Maisie, guided by antiques expert Ben Cooper. Their opponents in blue are mum and daughter Denise and Amy, with expert Gary Pe. Alan kicks off the reds’ shop by picking out a contemporary glass vase, but Ben doesn’t see a profit in it. Meanwhile, a pair of miniature wooden doll's chairs catch Denise’s eye, but does Gary think they’ll bring a big return? Down the road from Castle Combe, auctioneer Tim Weeks gives Christina his estimates of the teams’ items. One bonus buy particularly impresses Tim, but will it fulfil its auction potential?

Also in this episode, how secure is your self-storage unit? The team hears from one customer whose unit was broken into. And in the advice clinic, the team heads to Mansfield to meet the second-hand car owner whose vehicle was subject to a recall – so why was she left facing a £1,000 bill when it broke down?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A trio of rundown flats in Glasgow, London and Bournemouth are given the wow factor by family-developing teams who know how to turn unloved properties into desirable homes.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion buckles up in a vintage American muscle car to take a spin around one of Britain’s fastest racetracks. At 1.85 miles long, Castle Combe in Wiltshire is a popular circuit for vintage racing cars and has hosted some of the world’s motor racing greats. Christina rides shotgun with noise-monitoring officer Dave Hensley to learn about the history of the track and why drivers need to have their wits about them as they navigate its hair-raising straights and bends. Motoring around an antiques fair in Devon are two teams of families. In red are dad and daughter Alan and Maisie, guided by antiques expert Ben Cooper. Their opponents in blue are mum and daughter Denise and Amy, with expert Gary Pe. Alan kicks off the reds’ shop by picking out a contemporary glass vase, but Ben doesn’t see a profit in it. Meanwhile, a pair of miniature wooden doll's chairs catch Denise’s eye, but does Gary think they’ll bring a big return? Down the road from Castle Combe, auctioneer Tim Weeks gives Christina his estimates of the teams’ items. One bonus buy particularly impresses Tim, but will it fulfil its auction potential?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Rav Wilding and Nick Stapleton are back, working with ethical hacker Jim Browning to fight live scams in action and stop people across the country from paying out. The team are on the trail of a group of cryptocurrency scammers, who claim that their victims have previously lost large quantities of now-valuable crypto. All they need to do to release the funds is pay a fee up front. But the victim in question is unreachable – and the ground team might be too far away to warn him.

programme.title: Dinosaurs: The Final Day with David Attenborough
programme.desc: David Attenborough brings to life, in unprecedented detail, the last days of the dinosaurs. Palaeontologist Robert DePalma has made an incredible discovery in a prehistoric graveyard: fossilised creatures, astonishingly well preserved, that could help change our understanding of the last days of the dinosaurs. Evidence from his site records the day when an asteroid bigger than Mount Everest devastated our planet and caused the extinction of the dinosaurs. Based on brand new evidence, witness the catastrophic events of that day play out minute by minute.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from the largest town in Dorset want to escape the urban sprawl to establish a new country life in Devon, and Sonali Shah is on hand to help them kick-start their property search. Sonali also learns the importance of the role local newspapers play in keeping their communities connected and informed.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Barbara, Gareth, Rebecca and Iain – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: 21st Century TV with Lucy Owen
programme.desc: Lucy Owen explores BBC Wales’s news and entertainment archives of 2004. She takes us through the events, headlines and memorable moments of the year from her perspective in the newsroom, with archive gems that include the innovative dog clean at the car wash. Siân James remembers the miners’ strike of 20 years ago. Chirk Castle holds an auction of memorabilia – did you bid for anything? Entrepreneurship is alive and kicking around the country, from the eagerly awaited Penderyn whisky launch to the Welsh-designed 'Celtic Wanderer' super caravan. Blacksmith Ann Catrin Evans talks us through her inspiration for her work in the new Wales Millennium Centre. Do you recall who bought the famous Dylan Thomas watering hole Brown’s Hotel in Laugharne? We also visit the Welsh-Italian gondola moored in Neath, witness the first snow since 2001, and enter the rap band Goldie Lookin’ Chain’s unique world.

Palaeontologist Robert DePalma has made an incredible discovery in a prehistoric graveyard: fossilised creatures, astonishingly well preserved, that could help change our understanding of the last days of the dinosaurs. Evidence from his site records the day when an asteroid bigger than Mount Everest devastated our planet and caused the extinction of the dinosaurs. Based on brand new evidence, witness the catastrophic events of that day play out minute by minute.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from the largest town in Dorset want to escape the urban sprawl to establish a new country life in Devon, and Sonali Shah is on hand to help them kick-start their property search. Sonali also learns the importance of the role local newspapers play in keeping their communities connected and informed.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Barbara, Gareth, Rebecca and Iain – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A trio of rundown flats in Glasgow, London and Bournemouth are given the wow factor by family-developing teams who know how to turn unloved properties into desirable homes.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion buckles up in a vintage American muscle car to take a spin around one of Britain’s fastest racetracks. At 1.85 miles long, Castle Combe in Wiltshire is a popular circuit for vintage racing cars and has hosted some of the world’s motor racing greats. Christina rides shotgun with noise-monitoring officer Dave Hensley to learn about the history of the track and why drivers need to have their wits about them as they navigate its hair-raising straights and bends. Motoring around an antiques fair in Devon are two teams of families. In red are dad and daughter Alan and Maisie, guided by antiques expert Ben Cooper. Their opponents in blue are mum and daughter Denise and Amy, with expert Gary Pe. Alan kicks off the reds’ shop by picking out a contemporary glass vase, but Ben doesn’t see a profit in it. Meanwhile, a pair of miniature wooden doll's chairs catch Denise’s eye, but does Gary think they’ll bring a big return? Down the road from Castle Combe, auctioneer Tim Weeks gives Christina his estimates of the teams’ items. One bonus buy particularly impresses Tim, but will it fulfil its auction potential?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Rav Wilding and Nick Stapleton are back, working with ethical hacker Jim Browning to fight live scams in action and stop people across the country from paying out. The team are on the trail of a group of cryptocurrency scammers, who claim that their victims have previously lost large quantities of now-valuable crypto. All they need to do to release the funds is pay a fee up front. But the victim in question is unreachable – and the ground team might be too far away to warn him.

His old coping mechanisms no longer work, and he’s forced to ask himself what he truly wants. A conversation with Luke reminds him what’s at stake and what actually matters. Meanwhile, Cat seeks clarity from her son, hoping to understand the future she wants for herself and her family.

programme.title: Making Life on Earth: Attenborough's Greatest Adventure
programme.desc: In 1976, David Attenborough embarked on his most ambitious project ever, Life on Earth. No-one had ever attempted a natural history series on this scale before, and David’s reputation was on the line. This is the remarkable story behind the BBC’s most famous wildlife blockbuster. A three-year, hair-raising odyssey around the world, travelling to 40 countries and filming over 600 species, including the famous mountain gorillas. First broadcast in 1979 and watched by 500 million people, it launched David Attenborough’s career as the most successful and influential wildlife film-maker of our time.

programme.title: Wha's Like Us
programme.desc: Sanjeev Kohli takes a humorous look at how films have shown Scots, the Scots character and stereotypes, celebrating some of our most memorable onscreen moments. Are we really as mean, parochial and up for a fight as the movies often make us out to be? Sanjeev examines which Scottish stereotypes have a whiff of truth and which ones should be fed to the Loch Ness Monster. Packed with great film clips from both famous classics and lesser-known cult gems, the programme features contributions from an impressive supporting cast list, including actors Kate Dickie, Clare Grogan, Gary Lewis, Denis Lawson, Alex Norton and Tam Dean Burn. From popular adaptations of Kidnapped and Rob Roy to war dramas such as The Great Escape, from the wily islanders of Whisky Galore to the dark urban humour of films such as Shallow Grave, we look at what stories these films have told the world about us, and what these characters can teach us about ourselves. We eavesdrop on tourists taking in the sights with an Outlander tour, drawn to visit Scotland through our most expensive ever drama production, and we celebrate an unexpected staple of Scottish cinema: Scottish men crying.

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: A determined Eddie tries to prevent Viv’s lies from blowing up, but his meddling has tragic consequences. Meanwhile, Scarlett is left torn when Kelly-Marie expresses her cynicism about Sam, Gillian's world begins to crumble when her secret is exposed, and Maggie is concerned about Lydia.

programme.desc: After his dream Norway job doesn’t go quite to plan, Richard just wants to hide away from the world. Sadly for him, Ken has other ideas - mainly forcing him to join the protest group fighting to save the local allotments.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Andrew and dad Terrence are spinning plates on the farm, and with their glamping pods, just as the latest member of the Glenn family arrives. Long days on the dairy shed build and an infection in Adam’s leg mean he is desperate for a new prosthetic. Meanwhile, Ally and fellow crofters set sail to the stunning volcanic Shiant Isles, where they must navigate steep cliffs to find and shear sheep.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie heads for Ben Ledi in the Trossachs to help with some high-altitude fieldwork. And 25 years on from the foot-and-mouth outbreak, Arlene finds out about a legacy that is helping today's farmers. Elsewhere, Rosie is in Gairloch Wester Ross to hunt for herring and find out how this over-exploited species is making a comeback. Leanna is in Fife, where she joins a team researching the movements of secretive snipe, and Cammy visits the Ayrshire couple determined to preserve and promote the Clydesdale horse breed.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: There is lots of planting for the plate at Beechgrove Garden as Kirsty Wilson and Brian Cunningham start growing a wide variety of edible produce. Kirsty is the first of the Beechgrove team to kick off work on her competition plot. Each presenter has been given a sense to appeal to in each of their competition borders, and Kirsty is planting things that will taste fantastic. She is also trying something new to Beechgrove: hops. Meanwhile, Brian provides an update on the veg he sowed at the start of the series and is in his rain garden checking on what survived this year's wet weather. There are all the usual handy hints, and there is a visit to Calum Clunie’s allotment in Leven.

programme.title: Leigh-Anne: Race, Pop and Power
programme.desc: This powerful documentary follows pop star Leigh-Anne Pinnock as she confronts her experience as the only black member of Little Mix, and as a black woman in the music industry. Leigh-Anne talks about the racism she experienced growing up. Both her parents are of Caribbean heritage, and Leigh-Anne identifies as black. She is also aware that having lighter skin and being a celebrity means she is in a more privileged position than others. Leigh-Anne embarks on her own very personal journey to understand how she can use her platform and privilege to combat the profound racism she sees in society around her. After she begins her journey, news of George Floyd’s death and the Black Lives Matter protests start to sweep the world. With the force of a global movement now behind her, Leigh-Anne confronts those closest to her and attempts to bring difficult conversations about black representation right to the top of the music industry.

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: When the Doctor arrives in Victorian London he finds a dinosaur rampant in the Thames and a spate of deadly spontaneous combustions. Who is the new Doctor and will Clara's friendship with him survive as they embark on a terrifying mission into the heart of an alien conspiracy? The Doctor has changed. It's time you knew him.

programme.title: The Green Planet
programme.desc: More kinds of plants are crammed together in the tropical rainforests than anywhere else on Earth. The result is astonishing beauty and intense competition - a plant battleground. New filming techniques allow us to enter the plants’ world and see it from their perspective and on their timescale. From fast-growing trees to flowers that mimic dead animals, this is a journey into a magical world that operates on a different timescale to our own.

programme.title: Mammals
programme.desc: The dark, a world of opportunity for mammals. More than two-thirds prefer the cover of the night, with some now returning to the safety of the shadows in order to avoid us.

programme.title: Dynasties
programme.desc: In Senegal, west Africa, live a group of chimpanzees led by an alpha male named David. He has already been alpha for three years - a time when leaders here are usually overthrown. To make matters worse, David has no allies - no-one to help him defend his leadership. As the dry season sets in, the group are forced closer together to survive. But David is now surrounded by rivals who all want his crown and are prepared to kill him for it. David faces brutal battles, has his world engulfed in flames and has to pull off an extraordinary act of deception. In a story of power and politics, can David overcome the threats to his leadership and hold on to the alpha position long enough to sire a possible future heir to his throne?

programme.title: Half Man
programme.desc: 2018. It’s Niall’s wedding day as he follows his estranged ‘brother’ Ruben into a barn, away from all his guests. Here, in an explosion of violence, Ruben brutally and shockingly attacks him. Understanding why proves to be the driving question of this drama as we are catapulted back through the decades.

programme.title: Forensics: The Real CSI
programme.desc: A mother calls 999. Her 11-year-old daughter has returned from staying at her dad’s house, saying that a stranger came into her bedroom in the night and sexually assaulted her. A forensic team immediately heads to the crime scene, and the house is examined for potential forensic evidence the suspect may have left behind.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: There’s no time for horsing around as two teams canter through an antiques fair at Wetherby racecourse in West Yorkshire. In red, and saddling up for some fun, are sisters Sharon and Hayley, with their expert Charles Hanson. On the blue team, brothers Harley and Joe are paired with expert Philip Serrell. With one hour on the clock, the reds close in on an item that’s on their shopping list – an enamelled scent bottle – but they turn their noses up when they learn the best price. Over with the blues, Phil tries to spice things up with a silver nutmeg grater. Sadly, the three-figure price tag puts them off, so they stop to consider another important question – which sauce they prefer on their chips! Meanwhile, Danny Sebastian is dishing up a challenge for fairgoers, asking them to identify a mystery metal object. It’s silver-plated with a plunger at one end and a perforated acorn-shaped bowl at the other. What could it be?

programme.title: Secret Garden
programme.desc: David Attenborough reveals how tawny owls, badgers, dormice and bumblebees have made a home in a beautiful woodland garden hidden at the bottom of a steep-sided Welsh valley.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Kelly Cates presents highlights of three Premier League matches. Manchester United face Liverpool at Old Trafford, with both teams fighting to secure Champions League football next season. Elsewhere, relegation-threatened Tottenham Hotspur travel to high-flying Aston Villa, whilst Bournemouth, another team hoping to secure European football next season, take on Crystal Palace.

programme.title: The Titfield Thunderbolt
programme.desc: Ealing comedy about a group of villagers and their battle to preserve the local railway line by running it themselves, an enterprise that goes well until they are sabotaged in a midnight raid by the rival bus company. Undaunted, they wheel out the Thunderbolt, an ancient exhibit in the village museum. Now all that remains is to put on a satisfactory run for the stickler of a government inspector.

programme.title: Whisky Galore!
programme.desc: Classic Ealing comedy about a whisky-laden ship that runs aground off the coast of the Outer Hebrides during the Second World War. The local islanders have depleted their supply of the amber nectar and are overjoyed at the thought of stocking up again. But it is Sunday, and the teetotallers object to making free with the unexpected cargo.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Snooker: World Championship
programme.desc: Coverage of day 17 of the World Snooker Championship at the Crucible Theatre, Sheffield.

programme.title: The Best Dishes Ever
programme.desc: Ainsley Harriott introduces a selection of classic recipes from some of the BBC's best-loved television chefs. These dishes will help when you are planning the perfect picnic. The menu includes Paul Hollywood's pork pies with quail eggs, a superb sandwich from James Martin and Ainsley's own mustard, bacon and onion tarts.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel invites members of the public to bring along their antiques for examination. Surprise finds in Witney, Oxfordshire, include a pair of seascapes brought over from Holland in a suitcase 100 years ago which prove to have been a good investment. There is also an album of watercolours unearthed at a jumble sale and now worth at least £10,000, and a bracelet of gold eggs.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin and his team of experts invite members of the public to bring their antiques to be viewed and valued, with an option to sell at auction.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jordan Banjo, Sian Lloyd, Nick Pickard and Ellie White take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael begins his journey at the Demilitarised Zone, the heavily fortified border that has divided the Korean peninsula since the end of the Korean War. From the track of a long-abandoned railway near the Imjin River, he explores one of the most tense frontiers in the world and reflects on a conflict that ended in ceasefire but never peace. From the DMZ, Michael travels south by rail into Seoul, arriving in a vast, fast-moving capital that has risen from the ruins of war to become one of the world’s most advanced cities. Exploring palaces and the restored Cheonggyecheon stream, he uncovers how tradition and innovation coexist in everyday Korean life. At the BBC’s Seoul bureau, Michael meets the news editor broadcasting news into North Korea, before sharing street food with a North Korean defector who poignantly describes the personal cost of division. Michael’s first Korean leg ends at Kukkiwon, the World Taekwondo Headquarters, where he discovers how Korea’s national martial art reflects discipline, resilience and a hard-won modern identity.

programme.title: Snooker: World Championship
programme.desc: Coverage of day 17 of the World Snooker Championship at the Crucible Theatre, Sheffield.

programme.title: The Great Escaper
programme.desc: Based on the true story of Bernard Jordan, an 89-year-old veteran of the D-Day landings, who in 2014 sneaked out of his seaside care home where he lived with his wife, Rene, to board a cross-channel ferry and attend the 70th anniversary commemoration in Normandy.

programme.title: Mud
programme.desc: Two young lads join a spirited mystery man’s quest to reunite with his one true love, unaware of the forces and feelings that must be faced. Acclaimed Arkansas-set coming-of-age drama.

programme.title: Half Man

programme.desc: A mother calls 999. Her 11-year-old daughter has returned from staying at her dad’s house, saying that a stranger came into her bedroom in the night and sexually assaulted her. programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: There’s no time for horsing around as two teams canter through an antiques fair at Wetherby racecourse in West Yorkshire. In red, and saddling up for some fun, are sisters Sharon and Hayley, with their expert Charles Hanson. On the blue team, brothers Harley and Joe are paired with expert Philip Serrell. With one hour on the clock, the reds close in on an item that’s on their shopping list – an enamelled scent bottle – but they turn their noses up when they learn the best price. Over with the blues, Phil tries to spice things up with a silver nutmeg grater. programme.title: Secret Garden

programme.title: The Titfield Thunderbolt

programme.title: Whisky Galore!

programme.title: The Best Dishes Ever

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel invites members of the public to bring along their antiques for examination. Surprise finds in Witney, Oxfordshire, include a pair of seascapes brought over from Holland in a suitcase 100 years ago which prove to have been a good investment. There is also an album of watercolours unearthed at a jumble sale and now worth at least £10,000, and a bracelet of gold eggs.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin and his team of experts invite members of the public to bring their antiques to be viewed and valued, with an option to sell at auction.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jordan Banjo, Sian Lloyd, Nick Pickard and Ellie White take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael begins his journey at the Demilitarised Zone, the heavily fortified border that has divided the Korean peninsula since the end of the Korean War. From the track of a long-abandoned railway near the Imjin River, he explores one of the most tense frontiers in the world and reflects on a conflict that ended in ceasefire but never peace. From the DMZ, Michael travels south by rail into Seoul, arriving in a vast, fast-moving capital that has risen from the ruins of war to become one of the world’s most advanced cities. Exploring palaces and the restored Cheonggyecheon stream, he uncovers how tradition and innovation coexist in everyday Korean life. At the BBC’s Seoul bureau, Michael meets the news editor broadcasting news into North Korea, before sharing street food with a North Korean defector who poignantly describes the personal cost of division. Michael’s first Korean leg ends at Kukkiwon, the World Taekwondo Headquarters, where he discovers how Korea’s national martial art reflects discipline, resilience and a hard-won modern identity.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel invites members of the public to bring along their antiques for examination. Surprise finds in Witney, Oxfordshire, include a pair of seascapes brought over from Holland in a suitcase 100 years ago which prove to have been a good investment. There is also an album of watercolours unearthed at a jumble sale and now worth at least £10,000, and a bracelet of gold eggs.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jordan Banjo, Sian Lloyd, Nick Pickard and Ellie White take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael begins his journey at the Demilitarised Zone, the heavily fortified border that has divided the Korean peninsula since the end of the Korean War. From the track of a long-abandoned railway near the Imjin River, he explores one of the most tense frontiers in the world and reflects on a conflict that ended in ceasefire but never peace. From the DMZ, Michael travels south by rail into Seoul, arriving in a vast, fast-moving capital that has risen from the ruins of war to become one of the world’s most advanced cities. Exploring palaces and the restored Cheonggyecheon stream, he uncovers how tradition and innovation coexist in everyday Korean life. At the BBC’s Seoul bureau, Michael meets the news editor broadcasting news into North Korea, before sharing street food with a North Korean defector who poignantly describes the personal cost of division. Michael’s first Korean leg ends at Kukkiwon, the World Taekwondo Headquarters, where he discovers how Korea’s national martial art reflects discipline, resilience and a hard-won modern identity.

When the Grandmaster Glitch's TV aerial breaks, he orders the Grimbots to take Lars's favourite landmark, the Eiffel Tower, and bolt it onto the top of Grim HQ instead. Bing gets scared that he's growing down and that if he keeps going he'll be as small as Charlie.

The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in a kitchen, where they watch a lady decorating cupcakes. When she is finished, she puts away all the cake decorations in cupboards and drawers around the kitchen, while the Twirlywoos look on with interest. When she leaves the room, they decide to put the cakes away too and hide them in different places around the kitchen until they are all gone. The lady comes back with a crowd of children and finds the cakes are missing. The children spot one of the hidden cakes and a treasure hunt ensues as they uncover them all. The Hooter calls the Twirlywoos home as the children eat their cakes, and now they really are all gone! Toodloo pumps up the Tea Machine, but all that appears on top is a tiny grape. The tea that comes out is just enough to fill Great BigHoo's cup and he drinks it all - only to find that there is none left for the others! Toodloo goes back to get more tea, but again she only gets enough to fill Great BigHoo's cup. Finally, Chickedy and Chick run over to operate the machine. They continue to pump it up until a whole bunch of grapes appears, and there is enough tea for everyone.

Later, the boys pretend to be pirates and go in search of another type of treasure. Aboard their pirate ships, they race across a vast boating lake. But who will make it back to shore first? And will they find the pirates' gold coins?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Talib is cooking a recipe that his mum has taught him - a colourful Tanzanian banana curry. After lots of chopping and mixing in the kitchen, Talib decorates a beautiful Tanzanian-themed table complete with gold animals. He also greets his friends with a greeting spoken in Swahili, a language spoken in Tanzania. Unripened bananas are an important ingredient in his curry, but not all of his friends are keen on the taste when they try it at first. Will they like the cooked dish?

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today's episode, Maddie is sending a letter in the post to the CBeebies house. She finds out how posting a letter works as she follows the letter's journey from the post box to the sorting office and finally to the house. Using a special infrared light, Maddie shows us how stamps are scanned to tell if they are first or second class. Next, she visits a factory where colouring pencils are made. She finds out how the coloured crayon inside is made from clay and, using her slow-motion camera, we see the wooden shaft of the pencil being made.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Diesel is a hearing dog for his teenage owner, Rayane, who is deaf. This means he doesn’t hear everything. Diesel is trained to listen out for important sounds that Rayane might miss. Diesel is Rayane’s ears. Together, they’re unstoppable! Diesel and Rayane are off to the park, where their football team are doing a sponsored fun run to raise the funds for a new kit. Diesel has a busy day ahead. First, he has to filter out all the sounds in the busy park to help Rayane find his friends Grace and Karim and the rest of his teammates at the start line. Then, he has to listen for the klaxon so he can let Rayane know the race is starting. He doesn’t want him to get left behind! Rayane’s football coach uses British Sign Language to communicate the rules of the race to the runners before they set off. Diesel has to run alongside Rayane and alert him to any danger or to anyone trying to get past. Karim is leading the field until he takes a wrong turn – and Rayane and Diesel set off in hot pursuit. Can they catch their friend and help him finish the race?

programme.title: Go Wild

As they get closer, they see how these miniature monkeys get their name - they have a beautiful, golden mane just like a lion! Next, Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet up with another colourful animal, the poison dart frog. These frogs come in many amazing colours, and they get to meet some blue coloured dart frogs. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how woodlice play an important role in the environment. They find out that they are very adaptable and can live in lots of damp and dark places. They learn that woodlice are one of nature’s cleaners, cleaning up things like old leaves and dead wood and helping to recycle nutrients back into the soil. On the way, they spot some woodlice in a compost heap and do the woodlouse walk!

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: It’s Sophie’s first day. She worries that she’s no good at football but feels like part of the team when she helps the others work together to create a fantastic new football kit.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this episode, CBeebies’ very own motorbike rider, Grace, looks back at some of her favourite machines that are electric, fast and useful.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: Miss Collie has some exciting news - the school has a new cook who will introduce new food at lunchtimes. The pups don’t like the idea that their food might change, and they fear everything else will change at the school too. They decide to do something about it!

programme.title: Love Monster
programme.desc: A half-asleep Love Monster exits his house and walks towards the green, passing snoozing citizens on the way. He notices that the whole of the green is covered with litter and snoring Fluffytowners. Love Monster remembers that yesterday was Woo Hoo Day and the whole of Fluffytown had a big party - which makes today the Day After Woo Hoo Day. Love Monster attempts to clean up all of the mess on his own as a nice surprise for his friends, but he struggles and soon realises that it is a very big job. He should ask for help! He wakes everyone up, saying if everyone picks up one piece of litter each, they can tidy up the green in no time. Elder Kitten says he knows just the song for the job. Love Monster and Elder Kitten lead the Fluffytowners in singing a funky, tidying up song as they each pick up a piece of litter to clean the green. Everyone takes their piece of litter to the recycling centre where they queue up to do their bit for the environment.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: The Octonauts help some fire ants build an escape route when a river floods their home.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Peter escapes a very chatty Mrs Tiggy-Winkle to go strawberry-raiding, he is surprised to be helped out of trouble by none other than the feisty old hedgehog herself!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee hosts a reunion for the first ever Squirrels he looked after. But the first ever Squirrels are older now and very similar to the Squirrels' parents. Does that mean that when the Squirrels are bigger, they will become like their parents, too?

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Everyone in Sweetwood has an itchy nose, itchy eyes or the sniffles, but they are not sick. Vida knows that something in Sweetwood is causing the symptoms and finally figures it out—flowers!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: It’s Banana's Big Supermarket Game Show, and Supertato is going head-to-head with Evil Pea to win a speedboat. Supertato spots the Cobs sabotaging the show, and when Evil Pea thinks she’s won the speedboat, she can’t get away because Supertato is holding it above his head!

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings are having fun playing in their homemade castle. Weasy wants to be a noble knight but takes his playing too far and destroys the ducklings' hard work. Can he make it up to them?

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Mojo and Bo have to carry Jackson’s big blue 'chicken' Ludwig (who definitely isn’t a chicken) to the country fair. But the easily-startled bird gets away from them - the chase is on!

programme.title: Bluey

programme.title: Piripenguins

programme.title: Bluey

programme.title: Balamory

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle has so much fun on a doggy playdate at Mr Willow's house that he decides to stay for a sleepover! The Brooklyn-Bells miss Waffle and can't wait for his return.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi wants to swim with both her dads, but Jake feels nervous in the pool. Rafi makes a wish, and suddenly they all have mermaid tails! Jake isn’t sure at first, but with Rafi’s help, he learns to flip his tail and swim. When the wish ends, Jake is back on his feet and feels braver than before. Rafi understands that everyone gains courage in their own time, and the family share a happy hug.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: At the wetland centre, JoJo and her friends Alfie, Raya, Jaxon and Isaiah find frog spawn. Gran Gran and Cynthia teach them about the life cycle of frog spawn to tadpole and frog. The friends want to see for themselves, so they each take it in turns to check in on the spawn. Once they’re fully grown, the frogs are found busy hopping all around. But JoJo manages to snap a quick photo of one and finish the life cycle project on the board.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Scarf Lady welcomes Sarah and Duck to her house full of scarves.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: The Clangers are visited by a rare, strange and beautiful creature - a moon whale.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa are playing when MeMo accidentally knocks over a flower and apologises. BaBa’s bouncy ball startles the Tweeties, so BaBa says sorry, but doesn’t mean it and continues to be boisterous. BaBa’s ball also upsets the Yummies. It’s only when the ball bursts in a prickly bush that BaBa feels genuinely sorry for the ball. BaBa realises that to be sorry, you need to mean it when you say it.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: Upsy Daisy gives her special stone to Igglepiggle to look after whilst she rides the Ninky Nonk. But Igglepiggle starts to play with the ball and forgets all about Upsy Daisy's stone! Makka Pakka finds the stone and gives it back to Igglepiggle so that he can give it back to Upsy just in time.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Sophie Ingle reads an inspiring story about dreaming big and choosing your own adventure.
